parsed.answer: All three evidence sources link RAD52 to break-induced replication (BIR). Source [4899981] states that at common fragile sites and telomeres cells switch to a RAD52-dependent form of break-induced replication (MiDAS), and source [4319844] describes telomeric MiDAS as RAD52-dependent, RAD51-independent DNA synthesis potentially mediated by BIR. Source [14332945] adds that mammalian RAD52 localizes to replication-stress foci and promotes restart of collapsed forks, the repair process the authors place within BIR. The claim that RAD52 is involved in BIR is therefore supported.
